newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLO curve steepens again as MM rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLO curve steepens again as MM rates ease.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were seen steepening further on Friday as domestic money market rates continued to ease after blowing out earlier in the week.

One OLO trader said the move started late Thursday, when the German market was hit by late profit taking ahead of today's monthly U.S. employment report. "We saw the Bund go down much more quickly than Bobls," she said.
"Today we have again some flattening but I have the impression the Bobl is rising again and the short end of the Belgian market is bid," she added.
By 1000 GMT, benchmark 10-year OLOs were unchanged at a yield of 5.62 percent.
Three month money market rates had, however, eased to 3.48/60 percent from 3.56/60 percent, and one-week repos had eased to 3.55/65 from 3.80/85 percent.
The steepening move could get a further boost next week, when the Treasury is due to hold an exchange auction featuring OLOs 8 and 4.
